🚀 **v0.178.0**: security fixes from 2026-05-03 audit - H1 H2 H3 landed. H1 (SQL pattern in trading.rs:151) - replaced format() with column name with two static UPDATE strings selected via if-else. The previous pattern was technically safe (column names were hardcoded constants) but lint-flagged because format()-into-SQL is a footgun. Refactor removes the smell entirely. H2 (no timestamp freshness on federation messages) - new is_timestamp_fresh helper in broadcast.rs with MAX_TIMESTAMP_SKEW_MS = 5 min, matching the existing /api/vault/sync window. handle_federation_hello + handle_federated_chat now reject any timestamp outside the now plus or minus 5 min window before doing further work. Defeats replay attacks where an attacker captures an old hello and re-injects it later. 5 new unit tests cover fresh accept past reject future reject epoch reject. H3 (FederatedChat handler never verified the signature it carried) - previously a trust-tier-2 server could send chat under any from_name with any signature value because the field was passed straight through to broadcast. Now - canonical message format fed_chat newline from_name newline channel newline content is signed by the source server. handler verifies sig against the stored pubkey of the source server. Unsigned or invalid messages are dropped with a logged warning. H4 (DM crypto silent downgrade to plaintext) deferred - needs UI work for the user warning modal. M1 unsafe-inline CSP M2 action whitelist M3 entity_id spoofing L1 binary signature L2 manifest signature also deferred. 201 tests pass (5 new freshness tests in)

🚀 **v0.191.0**: v0.191.0 four operator-reported UI bugs - chat header full width + nav separator no longer doubled + channel save applies locally + avatar userbox is a fixed square. ONE chat header dark-gray bar only spanned the left portion of the center panel - to the right of the channel description was a black void going to the right panel boundary. Root cause - egui::Frame around the header wraps a ui.horizontal block which by default shrinks to its content's bounding rect. Frame paints based on what its inner UI claimed so a short channel description left a long stretch of unpainted background. Fix - first line inside the horizontal closure now calls ui.set_min_width(ui.available_width()) which forces the horizontal Ui to claim the full panel width. Frame inherits the claimed rect and paints its dark-gray fill across the entire bar. TWO main menu nav separators rendered with different visual thicknesses - the top tier-to-sub tier separator looked like 2px RGB + 2px gray while the sub tier-to-page separator looked like 1px RGB + 1px gray. Operator suspected doubling - actually a layering issue. Each TopBottomPanel by default draws a 1px gray separator line at its bottom. The rgb_separator panel below it then paints a nav_separator_height (3px default) colored bar. 🚀 **v0.201.2**: v0.201.2 cosmos-architecture doc - replace chunk-coord position model with continuous galactic DVec3. Operator pushback (2026-05-10) - "Why do we have to do cubic chunks instead of relative positioning? Like, why should we have a bunch of chunks between our solar system and the next? Wouldn't the main limitation of a cubic grid prevent the galaxy or solar system from naturally orbiting?" Operator is correct. The chunk model was solving three problems (procedural rogue seeding + sparse mutation persistence + spatial queries) but I'd conflated those with the position-addressing model itself. Precision was NEVER about chunks - f64 in light-years gives sub-mm precision even at 100 kly galactic radius. Orbits were NEVER about chunks - body positions are continuous functions of orbital parameters + sim_time, computed not stored. Inter-system travel was NEVER about chunks - just a vector that updates continuously between Sol and the destination. Revised model. ContainerRef::Deep now holds galaxy_pos_ly: glam::DVec3 (continuous 3D position in light-years from galactic origin) instead of chunk_coord: [i64; 3]. No chunks anywhere in the data model. Chunks become an INTERNAL implementation detail of the procedural rogue generator and sparse mutation persistence (presented as "modifications keyed by quantized position" rather than "the universe is divided into chunks"). Position composition unwrap for Deep is now trivial - `galaxy_pos_ly` IS the absolute galactic position no further math needed. Fleet jumping to deep space now updates galaxy_pos_ly continuously like any physics simulation - no discrete chunk boundary crossings. Inter-system travel is a vector that interpolates between Sol's (0, 0, 0) and Alpha Centauri's (-1.348, -3.972, -1.535) ly. Section 10 rewritten - octree-on-systems (Layer 1, internal index) + Poisson-disc-noise-field-for-rogues (Layer 2, deterministic procedural function with internal voxel caching). "Why this is better than the chunked model" subsection explicitly captures the operator pushback + the conflation it untangles. Precision-budget table updated - frame-relative units at each scale (meters in vessels, meters in systems, light-years in Deep). f64 still gives ample precision at every scale because each local_pos is expressed in units natural to its parent frame. Scattered chunk references throughout the doc (sections 3 / 4d / 5 / 7 / 9 / 13 / 14 / 17a / table headers) all updated to match the new model. cargo check still green - no code changes, just a doc patch. 🚀 **v0.205.0**: v0.205.0 cosmos page zoom fixes - multiplicative zoom + zoom-toward-cursor + Focus button + sidebar/moon-click auto-focus. Operator pushback 2026-05-10 - "Zooming in much further from this point is very slow where we're closest to Earth. Also zoom always seems to zoom to the sun. What are our options for choosing where the sun zooms into?" Two real bugs + a UX win. ONE multiplicative zoom replaces additive. Old code did state.cosmos_zoom += scroll_delta * 0.005 which means at zoom=50 each scroll tick is +0.005 absolute = 0.01% relative - basically invisible. New code state.cosmos_zoom *= 1.0015.powf(scroll_delta) which gives the SAME percent change per scroll tick at every zoom level (~1.08x per typical 50-pixel scroll). Feels responsive at 0.1x AND at 50x. Clamp range expanded 0.05..200x to allow deeper zoom. TWO zoom-toward-cursor. Standard map-UI convention - the point under the cursor stays anchored during zoom. Without this every zoom-in re-centers on whatever happens to be at canvas center (the Sun by default). Math - cursor_offset = cursor - rect.center(); ratio = zoom_after / zoom_before; new_pan = cursor_offset * (1 - ratio) + old_pan * ratio. Derivation - if a body's screen position is center + pan + world_pos * zoom and we want the cursor's world_point unchanged then solve for new_pan keeping cursor fixed. Pan applied BEFORE zoom in the same frame so cursor-anchored math uses the latest pan. Combined with multiplicative zoom this lets you scroll-zoom into Earth or any other body just by hovering over it - no manual panning required. THREE explicit Focus button in the right-side details panel. One click centers the map on the selected body. Useful when the user has zoomed in elsewhere and wants to re-target without panning. Also useful for jumping between bodies via the sidebar. New cosmos_focus_request: Option<String> on GuiState. When Some, the next System view render (after planets are positioned) computes the pan needed to translate that body's screen position to canvas center, applies the shift to cosmos_pan, clears the request, requests a repaint. For moons (which live in the cosmetic ring around their parent and arent in planet_positions), the resolver falls back to focusing on the parent planet - which is what users expect since the moons true 3D position relative to its planet is meaningless in the current top-down 2D scheme. FOUR sidebar body click + moon sublist click both auto-trigger Focus in addition to setting the selected body. Click "Earth" in the celestial bodies tree -> map centers on Earth. Click "Phobos" in Mars's expanded moons -> map centers on Mars (since Phobos lives in the cosmetic ring). The user explicitly indicated interest by clicking the body name; following up with a re-center is the natural UX. Map clicks in the System view stay select-only (don't auto-focus) because the user already pointed at the body with their cursor - re-centering would be redundant. cargo check + theme_token_lint + theme_editor_coverage + icon_glyph_lint all green. · [Release notes](<https://github.com/Shaostoul/Humanity/releases/tag/v0.205.0>)
